steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: I said, you can't go in.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: And I said I'm with Rhine Lab. I know the access rules for Propeller Paradise facilities better than you do, and no special permission is required to visit Cloud. It's a restaurant.

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: You would be correct under normal circumstances, but there is an important guest here right now.
Let him in. I think this young man's looking for me.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I take it the debriefing on the Rhine Vivarium incident is done?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Nothing gets past you.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I just happen to know a few people who are committed to Columbia's great project here.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Including Gordon Tannen?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I guess you're not here to try to recoup Rhine's losses.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: There isn't enough time before the exhibition now, even with emergency funding.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Please take a look at this inspection report.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: A tech startup solved a technical flaw that was discovered during inspections and received permission to stay on Propeller Paradise... what's the problem?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Lucky Cystybeast never passed the re-check. They have to leave Propeller Paradise today, according to the rules.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: But I just saw their owner and discovered that they solved the energy problem that had plagued them for months.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: On the eve of the exhibition. Deadlines, science, miracles... classic potato chip flavors, so to speak.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: No, look at this page—

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: I focused on several components that are not involved in standard inspection, and found that their output is more than ten times the standard values. Well, to put it in simpler terms—

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You don't need to explain technical terms to me. I wrote the Manual of Columbian Originium Component Standards you're carrying.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Do you mean to say that Lucky Cystybeast 'invented' power components far exceeding national standards in the span of a few hours?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Invented? They don't have the chops for that. I think someone transplanted a non-Columbian heart into that failure.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You know the rules of Propeller Paradise. All Terran eyes are on our progress in levitation technology. All the parts involved must be made in Columbia to ensure security.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: I'm not accusing the ATAO of negligence.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: No ordinary officer could have let a corporation dodge Rhine's regular and random inspections, unless someone manipulated the Engineering Section's inspection order.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Coincidentally, Director Lunorey came to an agreement with a certain official...

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Gordon Tannen.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: He would stop at nothing to tie Rhine's hands, because we are the true original proponents of Propeller Paradise, and the Engineering Section is a pair of eyes that could uncover his secret at any time.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: So you're speculating that Gordon Tannen has been running a smuggling operation behind the scenes?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: That is a serious accusation, young man.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: And it's why I had to come to you, sir.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Until Propeller Paradise gets to D.C., you are the only one in the position to deal with your 'diligent' subordinate.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I'm curious. Does your supervisor know about this?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Things wouldn't have come to this, if Director Lunorey did anything...

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You're a sharp, brave young man. Nasti wouldn't have let you stay behind to spend time with me if she knew.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Sir—

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I'm the only one in the position to deal with Gordon... an interesting way to put it. He used to butt heads with me, true, but that's the folly of youth, and true enough of you too.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: The first thing I ever taught him was that we'll always be of one mind when we stand for Columbia.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Hey...!
The young Rhine researcher can only watch as Gustave takes the report and turns to walk into the interior of the restaurant.
He is shocked and angry. He wants to charge at Gustave, but the man makes a simple gesture, and bodyguards twist the young scientist's arm, causing him to cry out in pain and frustration.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Hello?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: ...Heh, what a coincidence.
Sky Jagger is taken outside by the bodyguards, not knowing whether he'll be thrown into one of the lower-level jail cells or locked away in some secret room.
He hears Gustave pick up the phone. The man must be calling Gordon Tannen now. Sky Jagger regrets not leaving a copy of the evidence for Nasti. If he could just get back to the Vivarium—
Suddenly, the pain is gone. The bodyguards let go of him and push him into the elevator to take him away from Cloud.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: Hey! You can hear me, right?

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: I swear, I won't say a word about Mr. Tannen's smuggling operation! We really didn't mean to barge into his collection!

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Take a break, Oakley. You keep going like this, they're gonna start getting ideas that the best way to shut someone up is to kill them.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: *sniff*...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Ugh, you're crying again? Don't worry about it, giving prisoners the silent treatment is normal.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: Sounds like you know your prisons...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Where do you think I got my silver tongue?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Even if I ran into a bunch of Archosauria who couldn't understand a word I was saying and had me surrounded with spears, I could still get my point across with nothing but winks and gestures.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: You really think we can get out of this jail?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Have you ever been to Bleached Wasteland?

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: No... I hear the sandstorms there tear through the toughest metal sheet, and rip flesh from bone in an instant.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: True. All the guides say it's off-limits for a reason, and no travel agencies take tours there.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: But I didn't want to assume it was impossible just because of hearsay.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: Don't tell me you actually went there... and you got out alive?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: It's a gray desert.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: The scorching sun reflects off the sand. You can see dark-purple cliffs in the distance beyond the dunes, and the cacti grow taller than either of us.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: It is a dangerous place, and you can't even tell what you're standing on when the winds rage. But the sands aren't nearly as sharp as knives.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: Incredible...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: My dad used to say that 'impossible' is just an excuse for the lazy and cowardly.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I learned from him, and became a guide unlike the others, one who dares to brave the unknown.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: You had a supportive father. I'm jealous.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I did...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: That's why you should pick yourself up, Oakley. I'll grant your wish, and my Banshee client's wish too. Our journey isn't over yet.

steps.name: Propeller Paradise Police
steps.text: Get up, both of you.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: Wh-What are you gonna do? Stay back!

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: ...What's going on?

steps.name: Propeller Paradise Police
steps.text: Come with me and don't cause any trouble. Mr. Tannen wants to see you.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: What did I say? This isn't the end.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Yes, I understand... I apologize for the trouble, sir.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Screw that condescending old fox! We've got a retirement age in Columbia for a goddamned reason!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I'm not his coffee boy anymore! And I'll be damned if I'll let him yell in my face over getting the sugar wrong!

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Mr. Tannen... Five-Four is going to burst if you feed it any more...

steps.name: Space Finbeast
steps.text: (Foams at the mouth)

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Hmph. You take over the feeding.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Not a single thing has worked out! We didn't get those meddling Rhine Lab eggheads out of Propeller Paradise, and now the old fox and Nasti's people know about my side hustle...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: And those two bastards showed up out of nowhere to ruin most of my Arts unit collection! There's stuff there you can't even get anywhere else!

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Arts unit... hustle...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: So... you were... smuggling, all that time that you were away on unexplained trips?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You think it's wrong to help tech firms find their footing in the sky?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: No, it's not my place to judge, but...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Why are you bringing those two intruders over? Are you planning to... deal with them?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: What's with the angst? I got bigger plans for them than just settling a score.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: No one can take Propeller Paradise away from me without evidence. The rest of my collection needs to be cleared ASAP, before anyone else can intervene.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You want them to smuggle the contraband out for you?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: But everything that enters or leaves Propeller Paradise is subject to stringent checks, even if you give an expedited order. Besides...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Besides, the existing channels are out of service because of Engineering's renovation work, and I can't wait that long.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: This is all nasty Nasti's fault for that energy system modification shit. Floating botanical units and Rhine's people are everywhere now.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Wait, Rhine...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Well, if they're gonna block off my routes, it's only fair that I borrow theirs.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You mean the engineering tunnel beneath the Rhine Vivarium, used to transport heavy equipment and construction materials?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Exactly. With the Vivarium on lockdown, nothing offers better cover than Rhine turf. I know where the old fox is, but Nasti...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I'll take care of Director Lunorey, sir, as long as you ensure the safety of the two intruders.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I'm confident I can distract her while you carry out your plan.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I only need one thing—the Banshee's bone pen that you confiscated from Ferne.

steps.name: Propeller Paradise Police
steps.text: Get a move on. Don't keep Mr. Tannen waiting.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: (Whisper) He's gonna have our heads for ruining his collection room!

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: (Whisper) Just paying money isn't so bad. The real problem is if he wants a 'deal'...

steps.name: Propeller Paradise Police
steps.text: We're here.

steps.name: Propeller Paradise Police
steps.text: I brought them.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Thank you, sir. You may return to your duties.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Mercia, my client—

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Unfortunately, it seems Mr. Tannen had nothing to do with your client's disappearance. I'll do my best to keep an eye out.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Where did that Banshee go...?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Just go through the door and forget about her for now. Make sure you do exactly what Mr. Tannen tells you, if you ever want to leave Propeller Paradise on your own two feet.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: What's he planning?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: He's going to make you an offer you can't refuse.
Sky Jagger's steps grow slower and slower. He used to dash through this corridor, and his colleagues laughed at him for being impatient.
How could he NOT be impatient?
He did not have the luxury of a traditional education, of having his path paved for him. His family circumstances forced him to waste too much time on things other than research.
But now, he stands on the shoulders of Rhine Lab, at the pinnacle of applied science in Columbia, about to touch the very dome that has witnessed a miracle.
There should not be any obstacles. No one has the right to hold back this great work.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: I must tell Director Lunorey about Tannen's secret... and apologize.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Footsteps? I thought all the researchers were evacuated.

steps.name: Tester A
steps.text: Does this thing come off at all? It looks like one of those centrifugal safety membranes that the revolving bar used.

steps.name: Tester B
steps.text: Don't touch it if you're not sure. We'll ask our new boss later.

steps.name: Tester A
steps.text: Is Nasti still in her office?

steps.name: Tester A
steps.text: I heard she was willing to lose the whole Vivarium to save us, and that grumpy kid.

steps.name: Tester B
steps.text: Shh, shut your big mouth. Nasti's a good person. That's all we need to know.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Grumpy kid... me?

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: Thank you for your time. I think this is the beginning of a beautiful partnership.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: You're Gustave's secretary? What are you doing here?

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: Ah, you must be Sky Jagger...

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: I've finished my business with Director Lunorey. Excuse me.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You're back.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: You apologized to Gustave?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: You gave up all of Rhine's engineering control and agreed to stop active inspections?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Rhine Lab has essentially withdrawn from the exhibition and will no longer appear on the catalogue?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: We'll need to store our experiment equipment here later. Come and help, if you have the energy.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Director...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: You knew I would screw up. You knew I was just an average Joe. That's why you kept me busy with inspections and botanical units, right?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: You were right. In the end, I'm just a musbeast in the gutter. I understood greatness, but I could never become part of it.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: To be forgiven, saved, protected... like all the testers here, I'm just an ordinary guy left in the dust. I wouldn't be here without your help.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I needed new employees and an aide, that's all.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I stayed with a group of pioneers when I first came to Columbia. They despised me for being a Banshee who couldn't use incantations. I despised them for their lousy hunting traps.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: There was no passivity in our interactions. We forgave each other, saved each other, and protected each other.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: As we do now. As it should be.
The Vivarium is quiet, but the presence of the testers seems to have changed this place of cold, metallic rationality.
A misshapen wire pull tab has been added to the microscope slide box's stubborn lid. A sheet of plywood hangs from the air-conditioning vent, making it a little less unbearably chilly.
A few 'watch out' notes are pasted on the glass door that Sky tends to run into when he is angry.
They remind him of his little sister—
The average, ordinary one who, in his eyes, must always be protected.
He has never turned around to look back at her, not since he witnessed the miracle.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: If moving forward means we can't look back, how do we make sure we're still walking the same path that we chose in the beginning?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: What meaning is there in progress if it leads to a future that has been curated for only a select few?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Why should ordinary people be left behind?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: I never took you for an orator, Director.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: All I do is state facts. Ask questions, find the solution, repeat.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Get moving, before you let big words and big ideals take you for a ride.
